title: Banking System (4 levels)
description_html:
Implement an in-memory bank that processes a list of queries [op, timestamp, args…] and returns one string per query.

Levels

  1. Level 1: accounts and balances
    • create_account(ts, account_id) returns "true", or "false" if the id exists
    • deposit(ts, account_id, amount) returns the new balance, or "" if the account is missing
    • get_balance(ts, account_id)
  2. Level 2: transfers and top spenders
    • transfer(ts, source, target, amount) returns the source's new balance; "" if either account is missing, they are the same, or funds are short
    • top_spenders(ts, n) lists the top n accounts by total outgoing money as "id(total)", ties by id ascending; accounts with 0 are included
  3. Level 3: payments with delayed cashback
    • pay(ts, account_id, amount) debits now and returns "payment1", "payment2", … (one global counter)
    • 2% cashback (floored) is credited exactly 86,400,000 ms after the payment
    • get_payment_status(ts, account_id, payment) returns IN_PROGRESS or CASHBACK_RECEIVED
  4. Level 4: merge accounts
    • merge_accounts(ts, a1, a2): balances and outgoing totals combine, a2's pending cashbacks move to a1, and a2 is removed
    • a2's old payments must still resolve when queried through a1

Constraints / rules

  • Timestamps strictly increase; up to 104 queries; amounts up to 109.
  • Every cashback due at or before the current timestamp must be applied before the operation runs.

Progressive round: each level unlocks after the previous one passes. Write level 1 so later levels extend it rather than rewrite it.

Source: PracHub "Banking System Simulation" (Anthropic CodeSignal pre-screen); also reported as an eBay industry coding assessment and a Meta AI-enabled round. Candidate-reported; exact wording varies between reports.
